response.sql: WITH bucket_counts AS (SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(*) AS bucket_count FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT bucket_count, bucket_count * 1.0 / SUM(bucket_count) OVER () AS share FROM bucket_counts), compared AS (SELECT bucket_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS all_bucket_average FROM shares) SELECT COALESCE(SUM(bucket_count), 0) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - all_bucket_average) AS average_excess FROM compared WHERE share > all_bucket_average;

assumptions.assumption: “That average share” in the excess calculation means the plain average across all buckets used as the cutoff.

alternatives.interpretation: If “that average share” means the average share of the kept buckets, their average excess over it is zero whenever any bucket is kept.
alternatives.sql: WITH bucket_counts AS (SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(*) AS bucket_count FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT bucket_count, bucket_count * 1.0 / SUM(bucket_count) OVER () AS share FROM bucket_counts), compared AS (SELECT bucket_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS all_bucket_average FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT bucket_count, share FROM compared WHERE share > all_bucket_average) SELECT COALESCE(SUM(bucket_count), 0) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM kept)) AS average_excess FROM kept;
